findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed that establishment is using a multi-purpose cleaning bleach for food-contact surface sanitizer, and not an appropriate bleach product for food-contact surfaces. PIC was informed, and should acquire the proper sanitizing product by the Follow Up date of 18 May 2026. Ensure that chemical sanitizing agents that are applied to food-contact surfaces meet EPA requirements for food safe sanitizers.
findings.citation_text: 7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria. Chemical SANITIZERS, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to FOOD-CONTACT SURFACEs shall: (A) Meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions), or (B) Meet the requirements as specified in 40 CFR 180.2020 Pesticide Chemicals Not Requiring a Tolerance or Exemption from Tolerance-Nonfood determinations.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: 1st REPEAT: Observed a wet wiping cloth stored on the prep table. PIC was educated that wet wiping cloths must be stored in sanitizing solutions between uses. CORRECTED: PIC moved the wiping cloth into the sanitizer bucket during the inspection. Ensure that wet wiping cloths are always stored in chemical sanitizer when not in use.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: Observed that the triple sink has a leak at the sprayer. PIC was informed and should repair by the next routine inspection. Ensure that all plumbing systems are maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed that the one-person bathroom trash can does not have a lid. PIC was informed that all toilet rooms used by women shall have a covered trash receptacle for disposal of feminine hygiene products, and PIC should correct this by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 5-501.17 Toilet Room Receptacle, Covered. A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Observed the following areas in need of repair or replacement:
(i) The acoustic ceiling tiles (the ones with small holes) in the cooking area and in the bathroom. Replace with smooth vinyl ceiling tiles.
(ii) The bottom shelf of the wood top prep table is missing connections to one of the legs so it is tilting; it is currently supported by an unused metal potato press. Repair the shelf or replace the table.
PIC was informed of these areas, and will have them repaired or replaced by the next routine inspection. Ensure that all production surfaces are smooth, durable, and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: THIS IS A FISRT REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the facility did not have signed employee health reporting agreements. During the inspection all employees signed a copy and the PIC filed the signed agreements in the office. Ensure that the signed copies remain at the facility and new employees sign the agreement.
findings.citation_text: 2-201.11(E) Responsibility of Permit Holder, Person In Charge, and Conditional Employees. Responsibility of food employees and conditional employees to report. (E) A FOOD EMPLOYEE or CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEE shall report to the PERSON IN CHARGE the information as specified under (A) of this section.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee did not wash hands before putting on gloves to begin preparing food. When the action was observed the employee was instructed to wash hands. Ensure that employees always wash hands before donning gloves.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food obtained from approved source.
findings.comment: Observed the facility was selling packaged desserts that were prepared in a private home kitchen. When asked about the source of the desserts the PIC pointed out each dessert that was prepared in the home kitchen. The inspector educated that foods prepared in private home kitchens cannot be sold at the facility. The required desserts were removed from the cooler during the inspection. Ensure that foods always come from an approved source.
findings.citation_text: 3-201.11(B) Compliance with Food Law. (B) FOOD prepared in a private home may not be used or offered for human consumption in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the following foods stored in the incorrect storage order: (1) Raw meat stored over cooked meat in the clear double door cooler; and (2) Raw eggs stored over various sauces in the prep cooler bottom. During the inspection the raw meat was moved below the cooked meat and the raw eggs were moved below the sauces. The PIC was educated that raw foods must always be stored below ready-to-eat foods. The inspector will follow-up on 6/2/2025 to check on storage order.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records.
findings.comment: Observed that the facility uses time-as-control (TAC) for the lettuce by the taco station at the cash register but they were not marking times. The PIC was educated that they must either record the time the food entered TAC (i.e., when the lettuce was removed from the cooler) or when it must be discarded. During the inspection the PIC filled out a TAC policy where they indicated they will use labels to track the time. The inspector will follow-up 6/2/2025 to check that the lettuce is being marked with the 4-hour TAC window.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.19(B)(3) Time as a Public Health Control. (B) If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours: (3) The FOOD shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the FOOD is removed from temperature control.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: Observed that ground beef was thawing submerged with water in the triple sink when the inspector arrived. The PIC was educated that food must be completely submerged and under running water to be properly thawed. The PIC turned on the faucet after being educated about the proper procedure. Ensure that foods are always thawed according to an approved method.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed the box of utensils by the taco station at the cash register is stored with the handles and food contact portions intermixed. The PIC and inspector discussed possible solutions. The inspector suggests moving the utensils into another container where they can be stored with the handles facing outwards. Ensure that utensils are always stored in a position that prevents contamination of food contact potions.
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Observed there was not a sanitizer bucket available when the inspector arrived. The PIC stated that the bucket had been recently dumped. They were reminded that sanitizer buckets must be available whenever food preparation is occurring. When asked to make the sanitizer bucket the PIC first added dish soap to the bucket. The inspector educated that sanitizer buckets should only contain sanitizer and water (ex. bleach (about a capful) and water testing between 50-150ppm). The soap was rinsed out and the bucket was made correctly. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are always available during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned: 

(1) The silver drying rack holding clean dishes across from the triple sink. 
(2) The floor underneath the dry storage racks.  
(3) The white drink shelves in the walk-in cooler. 

Ensure that the above referenced non-food contact surfaces are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Several mouse droppings were observed under a dry storage shelf where skittles and Lipton tea drinks are stored. Ensure under shelving is cleaned to remove the current accumulations of droppings. Be sure to seal all gaps that act as entry points for pests and continue to clean as frequent as necessary to prevent accumulation. 

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: Several mouse droppings were observed under the dry storage shelves where the skittles and Lipton green tea are stored. The mouse droppings appear to be fresh. Ensure under shelving is cleaned to remove the current accumulations of droppings. Ensure pet control is contacted to let them know the issue and have them continue treatment of the facility. A follow-up is being issued for 8/21/24 to allow for treatment and cleaning to take place.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: Observed facility to not have any paperwork related to sick policy and reporting agreements. Paperwork was provided during the inspection. Employees were educated and documents were signed. Paperwork should be available for future inspections. 

(O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: Observed no Norovirus policy in place. Provided paperwork during the inspection. Keep paperwork available and educate staff on proper vomit cleanup. 

 A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
2-401.11: Observed an employee snacking on fries and drinking from a plastic water bottle. Educated them on proper eating and drinking in the food prep areas. They can drink from a container with a lid and straw in the kitchen, but must wash hands if drinking from a bottle. Do not eat in the kitchen. Discussed with staff at the point of observation.

(A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS.

 (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.comment:
3-501.16: Observed squeeze bottle of garlic parmesan to be stored on top of the prep cooler. Label on the bulk container indicated that product should be refrigerated after opening. Squeeze bottle was moved inside the prep cooler. If you would like to keep it on the counter, call the company and see what they would recommend. 

(A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Inspector did not observe any date marking on mashed potatoes and mac & cheese that were individually portioned from bulk. Prepared products held for longer than 24 hours must be properly date marked to indicate when prepared and/or a date by which to discard. This date marking must be consistent. The operated stated the product was from yesterday. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-302.12: Observed the facility did not have a stem thermometer. Provide stem thermometer and use it to monitor temperatures. 

(A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

findings.comment:

(A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLE shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination.

Discard and replace spatula so no plastic pieces fall into the food. Thick frost in the freezer prevents proper cleaning. Cardboard boxes also prevent proper cleaning.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM ROUTINE INSPECTION DATED 12/6/2023.

Inspector observed an operator use their phone and return to food preparation without washing hands. Glove use IS NOT an alternative to hand washing. Ensure that staff are washing hands as frequently as required by 2017 FDA Food Code. A follow-up is issued for 12/14/2023.

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Food separated and protected

THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS ROUTINE INSPECTION DATED 12/6/2023.

Inspector observed improper storage order in the upright cooler between the utility sink and the fryers. Raw fish was stored above RTE onion. Proper storage order is required to prevent contamination. Inspector discussed proper storage order with staff and will provide handouts. Ensure that proper storage order is maintained at ALL TIMES to prevent cross contamination. A follow-up is issued for 12/14/2023.

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS ROUTINE INSPECTION DATED 12/6/2023.

Inspector incidentally observed a container of shrimp thawing in a metal container in the utility sink as was observed previously. No running water was being used to properly thaw the shrimp. An approved thawing method must be used AT ALL TIMES. A follow-up has been issued for 12/14/2023 due to the nature of the violation and failure to cease the behavior. 

3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS ROUTINE INSPECTION DATED 12/6/2023.

Mop water was observed sitting in both mop buckets in the bathroom. Waste water must be immediately dumped after use and not allowed to sit in the facility. A follow-up has been issued for 12/14/2023 to ensure compliance with waste water removal requirements. Ensure that waste water in mop buckets is immediately dumped after cleaning is completed and before returning to food preparation. 

5-402.13: SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
The person-in-charge on arrival to the facility was not able to verify that he was a certified food manager through the provision of a certificate. When asked if he was the certified food manager, he stated no but that the certified food manager had just left. When asked if he had a CFM certificate he claimed that he did but was unable to find it. Person-in-charge was unable to answer basic questions regarding operations of the facility and did not take responsibility for the operations when asked. Additionally, the facility has been cited for multiple repeat violations and numerous priority/priority foundation violations during the inspection today. A person-in-charge who denies responsibility for the facility cannot, by definition, demonstrate active managerial control of the facility. A 30-day follow-up is issued to ensure compliance with all priority/priority foundation items and that active managerial control is achieved at all times. Inspector will return on January 8, 2024.

2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECITON ON 04/12/2022. 

The person-in-charge of the facility on arrival stated that he is a certified food manager but is unable to provide any documentation showing completion of the course and examination from an accredited program. As such, inspector is left to assume that the person-in-charge is not a certified food manager. A certified food manager arrived to the facility later in the inspection correcting this violation. A certified food manager must be present during all times of operation. Ensure that certificates are available for all certified food managers to verify compliance. Corrected on site. However, due to repeat violations of this requirement and numerous priority/priority foundation violations, a follow-up is issued for Monday 12/11/2023.

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
Staff were observed drinking from plastic bottles in the kitchen and near the food prepared in the cashier area during the inspection. Drinking may not occur anywhere food preparation and/or service is occurring UNLESS drinks are kept in containers with lids and straws and kept away from consumer food. Ensure that personal food/drink is not consumed in any food service areas of the facility.

2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Inspector did not observe ANY hand washing occurring during the inspection despite staff switching tasks repeatedly. Gloves were used but gloves are not a substitute for hand washing. Hands must be washed any time that contamination may have occurred. Ensure that staff are washing hands at the required frequency. A follow-up is issued for Monday 12/11/2023.

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTIONS DATED 4/12/2022 AND 12/20/2021. A NOTICE TO COMPLY WILL BE ISSUED BY SCDPH SUPERVISOR AND FAILURE TO BRING THE FACILITY INTO COMPLIANCE WILL RESULT IN ADDITIONAL ENFORCEMENT UP TO SUSPENSION/REVOCATION OF PERMIT.

Inspector observed three hand sinks in the facility. The first hand sink observed in the kitchen is in the corner to the left of the cooler/fryers and was not stocked nor designated for hand washing and contained improperly thawing shrimp. The second hand sink was to the right of the fryer and behind a metal table completed inaccessible and dry indicating it has not been used. The last hand sink was in the bathroom which was stocked with hand soap but no paper towels. None of the three hand sinks were properly stocked and/or accessible to employees to ensure hand washing is occurring. Facility was provided with hand washing signs and have chosen to designated the right hand sink and bathroom hand sink as designated hand sinks. Operator is aware that these hand sinks must be COMPLETELY accessible and stocked at ALL TIMES to facilitate appropriate hand washing. A follow-up for stocked/accessible hand sinks is issued for 12/11/2023.

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION DATED 12/20/2021.

Raw chicken in the coca cola cooler and on the far left (from front) rack of the display cooler was observed to be stored above shrimp, onions, fish, and ground beef. Foods must be stored in the proper order to prevent cross contamination of foods which cook to lower required temperatures. Chicken (and raw shelled eggs) should be stored at the bottom of the cooler. Ensure that proper storage order is used at all times. A follow-up is issued for 12/11/2023.

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
During the inspection, no sanitizer was used to wipe counters and other surfaces. After pointing out specific sources of contamination of food contact surfaces such as a personal phone on a cutting board surface, no sanitization occurred. An unlabeled metal container with a metal scratch pad was the source of sanitizer at the rear of the facility for ware washing but was not sufficiently large to submerge dishes. Purell sanitizer spray was in use for surfaces however employee had to look for this sanitizer and was unsure where it was when asked. Additionally, no test strips are available for alcohol solutions such as Purell. A follow-up is issued for 12/11/2023 to ensure that sanitizer is properly prepared in a labeled container and available for use on all surfaces and actively being used to sanitize surfaces.

4-702.11: UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Inspector did not observe any date marking on thawed products in the cooler. Thawed, prepared products held for longer than 24 hours must be properly date marked to indicate when thawed/prepared and/or a date by which to discard. This date marking must be consistent. When asked if the product was cycled within 24 hours, operator responded by saying that the product usually used within 24 hours. Usually means that the item is not consistently used within a 24 hour period and must be date marked accordingly. A follow-up is issued for 12/20/2023 for date marking within the facility.

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Chemical sanitizer was kept in an unlabeled metal container with no distinction between the sanitizer container and containers used for food service. Ensure that sanitizer is labeled properly (bleach) to ensure that all individuals at the facility are aware of what is kept within the container. A follow-up is issued for 12/20/2023 to ensure that sanitizer is labeled properly.

7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the thawing of shrimp in a metal container in the utility/hand washing sink to the left of the fryers/cooler. Utility sinks used for mop buckets and dumping are not appropriate for thawing of foods. Additionally, foods thawed in water must be retained below 41 degrees in running cold water. The water in the sink was not running on arrival. Ensure that proper thawing occurs at all times. 

3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
Per operator, probe style thermometers are not available. Facility possessed an infrared thermometer which has been lost. As such, the facility has no means of ensuring that foods attain the proper temperature when cooking or that held foods are maintained at the correct temperatures. Ensure that probe style thermometers are available. A follow-up is issued for 12/20/2023 to ensure the available and use of thermometers for checking food temperatures.

4-302.12: (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION ON 4/12/2022.

Foods are observed to be stored on the floor throughout the facility. Foods in the consumer area of the facility are observed on the floor and include picks, candies, deserts, and other foods. Inspector observed meat and produce stored on the floor in the walk-in cooler. Packages of chips used for the preparation of nachos for service are stored on the floor of the upper cashier area. Foods may NEVER be stored on the floor of the facility except those in pressurized beverage containers (soda), cased food in waterproof containers and milk containers in plastic crates. Ensure that foods are stored at least 6 inches above the floor at all times.

3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM INSPECTION DATED 4/12/2022.

Open containers of food are stored in two chest freezers at the rear of the facility with a significant amount of ice accumulation touching permeable packages of food. Chest freezers must be kept clear of ice accumulations when storing foods within. Ensure that these freezers are defrosted/scraped and remain free of ice accumulations. 

3-303.12: (A) PACKAGED FOOD may not be stored in direct contact with ice or water if FOOD is subject to entry of water. (B) unPACKAGED FOOD may not be stored in contact with undrained ice. (C) Whole raw produce, cut, raw vegetables such as celery, carrots, potatoes, or tofu can be immersed in ice or water. (D) Raw poultry and raw FISH received in ice may remain in condition while in storage awaiting preparation, display, service, or sale.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Single use forks were observed to be stored in an open box on the floor of the upper cashier area. Operator states that these forks are not used however the are stored directly next to chips on the floor used in the preparation of food and thus the assumption has to be made that if these items are stored in the food service area, open and available for use, that they are being used in the facility. Single-use items must be stored at least 6" off the ground and protected from contamination at all times. Ensure that single use items are stored properly.

4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: Facility possesses a triple sink but is observed using a small metal container for sanitizing dishes which is not sufficiently large to handle soiled equipment/utensils. Basins used to sanitize dishes in the facility must be sufficiently large to accommodate equipment and utensils. The basin of the triple sink is large enough but has no sanitizer in it and operator confirms that the small metal container is used for sanitizing dishes. An appropriate wash, rinse, sanitize setup must be setup during operations. Ensure that the proper warewashing setup and equipment are used during operations.
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. 
(B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.comment:
Mop buckets are stored in the bathroom with mops stored in the heavily soiled water in the bottom portion of the mop buckets. Waste water must immediately be conveyed to the sewage system of the facility and not permitted to sit in mop buckets after mopping has been completed. Ensure that the mop bucket waste water is disposed of properly and immediately after mopping. A follow-up is issued for 12/11/2023 to ensure that mop water is removed from the facility.

5-402.13: SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Sinks in the facility are not caulked to the wall. All equipment against walls which are not easily moved must be sealed to the wall to create a smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable surface. Ensure that all sinks and other equipment are sealed properly to create easily cleanable surfaces. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed mops stored in soiled water in the bathroom. Mops must be stored in a manner that prevents contamination and facilitates air drying. Allowing mops to sit in soiled water contributes to microbial growth and the spread of bacteria and other possibly hazardous materials. Ensure that mops are stored properly.

6-501.113: Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Upon entry to the facility, inspector observed a strong paint odor. Inspector observed spray painting occurring in a back room with the door left open repeatedly. There is not sufficient ventilation within the facility to prevent noxious odors and fumes from accumulating within the consumer areas of the facility and within the kitchen. Ensure that the facility is properly ventilated to prevent fumes from accumulating inside. 

6-304.11: If necessary to keep rooms free of excessive heat, steam, condensation, vapors, obnoxious odors, smoke, and fumes, mechanical ventilation of sufficient capacity shall be provided.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM INSPECTIOND ATED 4/12/2022. 

Food handler certificates are not available for staff upon request by inspector. 

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
There was no CFPM at the establishment during the inspection. Class information was provided during the inspection. 
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed the cook line hand sink blocked by a prep table and trash can at the start of the inspection. The trash can and prep table was moved so it was accessible during the inspection. Ensure the hand sink is accessible at all times. 
5-205.11:  (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: The hand sink in the cook line did not have paper towels at the start of the inspection. Paper towels were provided during the inspection. Ensure paper towels are provided at each hand sink. 
Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the can opener to be soiled with old food debris. Ensure the can opener and other food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch. The can opener was moved to the 3 part sink for cleaning.
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Observed boxes of chicken and other foods stored on the ground in the walk in cooler. Ensure foods are moved and stored 6 inches off the ground to protect food from contamination. 
3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Observed the chest freezers in the establishment to have an accumulation of frost, which makes them not smooth and easily cleanable. Ensure frost is removed so the freezers are smooth and easily cleanable. 
4-101.11: (A) Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be safe. findings.comment:
Observed the sani bucket to be filled with soap and water. Ensure there is a sani bucket with sanitizer inside it available for use during all hours of food prep and operation. The sani bucket was filled during the inspection with sanitizer solution. 
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Observed an employee’s fried chicken sitting on the top rack of a shelf in the walk in cooler. Personal food and items must be stored separately from food sold by the establishment. Storage options were discussed with the manager.

6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur.

Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: Observed shrimp and chicken stored above sauce and other ready to eat foods in the sliding door cooler. Ensure Proper storage orders are followed with ready to eat food being above meats and seafood stored above chicken. The foods were moved to the proper storage order during the inspection.
